literal_source_claim: The L^2 Fourier transform is an isometry.
canonical_claim: For every finite dimension n and every complex-valued square-integrable function on real Euclidean n-space, mathlib's normalized L^2 Fourier transform preserves the L^2 norm.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat; f : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n) -> Complex; hf : MemLp f 2 volume; Prop in Lean universe 0. The normalization is the one fixed by pinned mathlib's Lp Fourier instance.
hypotheses: hf certifies square-integrability with exponent 2 and volume measure
conclusion: The L2 norm of the Fourier transform of hf.toLp f equals the L2 norm of hf.toLp f.
excluded_degenerate_cases: The zero-dimensional space is included. Infinite-dimensional spaces, arbitrary LCA groups, non-L2 functions, real-valued codomains, and unnormalized transforms are excluded.
